lines.english: It's Sunday.
As usual, I woke up, changed my clothes, washed my face, and went to the apartment next to mine.
…But unlike what I usually do, my finger stopped right before I could press the doorbell.
"Before you make up with Setsuna… allow me this, just once."
It's still there.
Kazusa's resigned smile.
Kazusa's voice, stripped of its thorns.
Kazusa's teary voice. The sensation of Kazusa's forehead on my chest.
And coming from Kazusa's hair, a faint smell of…
A faint smell of… burnt food?
"But why…?"
"I did it the same way Haruki does it…"
"Kazusa! Kazusa! What happened in there!? What the hell are you doing!?"
"I'm cooking!"
"…It's cold."
"Wait until the fresh air comes in."
The first sensation that came to me the moment I bolted into the room wasn't something I could see, but something I could smell.
I opened the window to let the smoke out, turned off the fire alarm to avoid making matters worse, surveyed the room, and then finally looked up at the heavens.
More specifically, at the insides of the frypan where the food itself has been colored pitch black.
"I never thought fried eggs could produce this kind of smell…"
"What are you talking about? It's clearly mixed with the smell of the toast!"
"Right…"
I turn my gaze to the toaster oven, from which black smoke is still rising.
A combination of carbohydrates and protein is getting burnt… No wonder it's suffocating in here.
"…Well?"
"Wanna have some? Breakfast, I mean."
"Don't eat that! I'll make something new."
I'm not sure whether she said that because she feels responsible for making that hunk of charcoal, or if it's because of her own bizarre palate, or if it's simply a show of frugality.
…Well, I'm sure it's not the last reason.
"Why would you start this all of a sudden? Your concert is right around the corner."
Yes, Touma Kazusa's opening concert in Japan is merely a week away.
I'm sure her practice hours will increase even further than now, giving her even less time to worry about anything else.
Yet despite that, Kazusa's actions suggest the complete opposite to the point that I have to wonder if she saw some weird dream…
"I thought I should try becoming more independent."
"Like I asked, why all of a sudden…?"
"It's unfair to Setsuna."
"…I told you that's irrelevant."
…But it's neither a dream, nor a false assumption of mine.
She told me to reconcile with Setsuna. To never let her go again. To put some distance between herself and me…
"Of course, we'll continue the coverage as usual, and I'll rely on you in case of any trouble. But we won't meet for any other reason from now on."
Kazusa's proclamation last night is being turned into reality before my eyes, standing between us.
"That doesn't mean you should turn your food into…"
"Yes, I was naive to think I could do everything on my own. I'll be good from now on and eat out."
"But then your nutritional balance…"
"I'll properly eat three meals a day. I'll eat vegetables too. I'll avoid sweet foods… I'll use that meal program you made as reference."
"I'll learn to bind my own hair. Teach me how to do it later."
She addressed everything before I could get a word in.
She made sure to shut down any proclamation of "don't worry about that" from me.
Kazusa has become really argumentative over the past few days.
I have a single complaint toward the person who ended up influencing her to become that way, if only I knew who they were.
I absolutely hate myself…
"Did Setsuna call you?"
"No…"
"I see… She's pretty stubborn, isn't she?"
"Because she hasn't found a reason to forgive me."
"But that's because you two promised that only Setsuna can call, isn't it? This is something that Setsuna has to overcome herself, isn't it?"
"That's…"
"I thought she got it out of her system with the concert yesterday. To think that Setsuna is still not…"
"It's fine. I'll wait until she calls me… After all, I made her wait three years."
"…Mhm. Good luck, Haruki."
Even me being encouraged by Kazusa is in many ways a strange subversion.
"I'll make sure to do my best for the remaining week I have. I'll get this job over with, and then I'll leave."
"…Are you serious?"
It's just that even as Kazusa makes declarations like these in order to save me, I can't accept them over the span of a single night.
"Even when the concert next week ends, you still have another concert in Japan, don't you? You have your additional concert next month…"
Kazusa will still remain in Japan for a short while longer…
"I'll be fine if I play once. My nervousness will go away and my mom will be relieved too."
"But that's assuming that the concert will be a success, isn't it?"
"What's the matter, Haruki? Do you want me to fail?"
"…Ah, no… Sorry."
What's the matter, Haruki…? Can you not answer "no" to that question without hesitation?
"Just kidding. I'll be fine. I'll succeed. I'll satisfy everyone coming to listen to me play, and I'll disappoint all the mass media coming to disparage me."
"Y-Yeah…"
"And after next week, I'll learn to live by myself… I'll learn to not depend on you."
At some point… or rather, since yesterday, Kazusa has come to acknowledge that she has been depending on me up until now.
On top of that, she has come to speak optimistically about independence with a confident expression.
I don't know if that's how she truly feels. I don't even know if I want that to be how she truly feels…
"Regardless, it's one more week. Finish your coverage until then. I'll tell you about anything you want to hear or write about."
"But you'll need more time to practice before the concert, right? Forcing you to do this now would be…"
"I told you I'm fine, so I really am. …Get it over with already."
"Kazusa…"
"Like I just said, I'll eat out from now on, so there is no need to come here to make food. Call me before coming over… only when you're doing interviews, I mean."
"…Your fried eggs are done."
One more week.
Once her first concert in Japan ends, we'll return to how we were a week ago… In a week, we'll go back to how we were "two weeks" ago.
But…
We can never return to how we were before our reunion.
"…Did something happen?"
"You're not giving me a score today."
"Well, it would be boring to. You've got everything down now, in a way that suits my tastes, no less."
"You told me to, didn't you? I'm only doing what's expected of me. Besides…"
"Besides?"
"I have a responsibility."
"To give a good performance to your Japanese fans?"
"It's nothing so ordinary. It's just that there is a person who would be sad if I didn't get it together… and I can't betray that person to that point."
"I see… then."
"By the way, that person is not you. And it's not the person you think it is either."
"No, I'm certain it's precisely who I think it is."
"I'll finish the first and second movements today. I'll have everything done completely three days before the concert."
"Even then, are you sure?"
"About what?"
"About leaving that apartment once your concert next week is over…"
"What would be the point in lying about that?"
"Why? You haven't even lived there for a month."
"Didn't I just tell you? I'm going to become independent."
"Are you capable of that?"
"I am capable. I'm an adult now. I won't need you to come along on my next overseas performance."
"Are you capable of giving up?"
"Forget giving up, I don't have any lingering feelings to begin with… No, wait, I mean, I don't know what you're talking about."
"Is that so?"
"It is. Anyway, break's over. Can you leave now?"
"Yes, yes. Do your best."
"No lingering feelings to begin with, she says…"
"And yet, the sound of her piano has gone back to oozing romantic frustration, hasn't it?"
"I might have told you this before, but I really don't know anything about my father. Not his name, or whether he's even still alive."
"I see…"
"Whenever I ask mom, she just laughs and never answers… Perhaps she doesn't even know herself."
"No, that would be…"
And in the evening…
Kazusa came home a bit later than usual, claiming to have eaten at a family restaurant.
She didn't call me or contact me through the intercom, so it took me a while to realize she was back home.
"From as early as I can remember, there was only mom and the helper in that massive house. It wasn't Shibata-san who was with us back then, but someone else."
When I noticed noises coming from the other apartment and called her, she responded with "Interview?" in an overly formal tone.
"I don't think I needed much attention as a kid. After all, I was playing around with the piano from dawn till dusk."
I might have felt a little frustrated at her uncertain response.
"…I wasn't playing with those kids' toys, you know? It was one of my mother's spare grand pianos."
"If Youko-san used it… it must've been extremely high-grade, huh?"
"I'm pretty sure it must've cost over ten million yen when she bought it. It was made by one of the big three piano makers in the world, after all."
I stepped on a taboo topic of Kazusa's to rile her up somewhat.
…I brought up the subject of her upbringing.
"You know about that, right, Haruki? About how we're as rich as people think we are."
I just wanted to make her angry.
Somehow, I just didn't like how composed she looked.
"Mom was already born in a rich family. Though I suppose you can't become a pianist if you're not. You need special education from childhood to succeed."
Even so, Kazusa wasn't intimidated.
She's giving a straight and direct answer to my spiteful, provocative question, causing me to feel daunted instead.
"But almost all the money she has now is what she's earned herself."
She's more talkative than I ever imagined she'd be, with a small amount of the same sarcasm she usually employs.
"Apart from being an outstanding pianist, Touma Youko was also a capable promoter, after all. She knew how to promote herself."
Touma Kazusa is laying bare her respect, scorn, love and hatred toward Touma Youko.
"She was very good at getting popularity above what her actual ability warranted. Though I suppose no one could complain, for that in itself was part of her ability."
She's talking about something that a gossip journalist would absolutely adore, to perhaps the person who abhors it the most.
"…No, there were plenty of people who complained about her and envied her, but she crushed them all with shady tactics."
"Shady tactics…?"
"She unsparingly used her womanhood as a weapon. Whenever we occasionally went out eating, there was always a different man sitting next to her."
I'm sure she's doing this on purpose…
The fact I've been wearing a scowl since halfway through her speech is proof of that.
"Of course, they weren't all Japanese. It was either some old geezer president from a big corporation or some younger man."
Again and again, she's carelessly throwing out valuable information that I have to note down despite the fact that I don't want to.
I want to refute her or speak in Youko-san's defense, but I know that nothing Kazusa is telling me right now is a lie.
"Thinking about it now, that woman probably saw men as either sugar daddies or gigolos."
She's willingly telling me this because she's obviously aware that I'm the only person who understands that.
"It's something I'm incapable of… I can't reach that castle of hers."
"It would be a problem if you did…"
She's definitely doing this on purpose.
"Are you sure… I can write about this?"
"I don't mind… that is to say if mom is okay with it of course."
"No, I'm pretty sure Youko-san wouldn't even bat an eye."
"…I think so too."
"She's really overprotective, isn't she?"
"You mean like how she's letting me say whatever I want like right now?"
"No… I meant like how she got her own hands dirty, and let you purely play the piano."
That goes even for Kazusa moving in here. She put herself and everyone around her in a whirlpool of confusion, all for her daughter's sake.
If that's not an overprotective parent, I don't know what is.
"Well, whatever. I'm sure life itself is a joke to her. She seems to enjoy being misunderstood like this, after all."
"A joke…"
"But you alone should understand her, no? Otherwise, Youko-san will never rest easy."
"Even though she's been dragging you along with so much nonsense. I'm amazed you can still defend her."
"I haven't lost my way yet. And besides, I'm only saying what I want to tell her myself."
Moreover, this isn't just me defending Youko-san. This is also my counterattack toward Kazusa.
"…I see. It's because you can say things like that to her family and herself with a straight face that she likes you."
"She likes me?"
"She likes you."
"Youko-san likes me…?"
"Anyone can tell by looking, Guitar-kun. …But, I refuse to call you my dad, okay?"
"…!? Pfft, cough! W-W-Wha…"
But today isn't going my way at all.
Kazusa is too much for me to handle, now that she looks like she's gotten over something.
"…Just kidding. You already have Setsuna, so that was a tasteless joke. Forget about it."
She constantly acts as if she has decided to specialize in making me feel awkward.
She has turned into someone a bit different from the usual Kazusa; someone a bit more cheerful than the usual Kazusa.
Without knowing why, I feel a twinge of sadness well up in me.
"Well, setting that aside… I never had any ill-feelings toward Touma Youko's adventures with men."
"Of course not. She raised such a spoiled daughter with the help of a single female worker. Why would you ever hate her?"
"The reason I despised her was because… Actually, you already know the reason… You and mom alone."
"Yeah, you hated her without any justification. You received a favor you could never return in your entire life, yet you repaid her with nothing but spite."
"I really am amazed that you can say that to people's faces with a straight face…"
"This attitude is the most effective one toward the Touma family, after all."
"That only goes for my mom. I'm different."
"Is that so? Well, my bad then…"
"I'm completely different… Don't be mean, idiot."
"…Like I'd know."
"You do know… You know everything about me."
Yet at some point…
Kazusa, who had the upper hand over me, started making the same expression as me.
"I sang for the first time in a year yesterday."
"In one of the regular concerts in Studio Troy. You've been there to listen once too, right, Haruki-kun? Tomo helped me get a spot as a backup singer."
"I was really nervous at first, but at some point my voice came out clearly. I think I have this kind of thing memorized in my muscle memory."
"There were even a lot of people who remembered me in the crowd. They greeted me very warmly, so maybe I got my confidence from them?"
"Because of that, I was completely absorbed in my performance from beginning to end."
"And when I finished singing, I felt like crying. For some reason, so many things started to well up in my mind."
"Being on the stage was so much fun."
"But the thoughts that welled up weren't all about fun things, so I started hating myself a bit."
"But when I was surrounded by the applause of everyone listening, I thought of forgetting about all that."
"I thought of forgiving you, Haruki-kun."
"Despite my self-centeredness, I thought of wanting to be forgiven by you too, Haruki-kun. If possible, in a gentle way."
"I wanted to see you again and let my feelings gush out without self-restraint. Including words that would cause you pain, Haruki-kun."
"And if we had a fight again because of that… No, I don't even want to imagine that, but I thought of talking it out again, and making up."
"…That's what I truly felt back then."
"Everything I'm about to tell you is pure fantasy, so don't worry about it. You don't have to respond either."
"After all, I think she was mistaken. No, I'm certain that she was mistaken, because that would be simply impossible."
"That's why, Haruki-kun, I want you to answer me honestly just one more time."
"You're not hiding anything from me, right? There are no secrets between us, right?"
"I can trust you, right?"
"What is this?"
"Did I… really write this?"
"About what you sent this morning."
"Yes."
"Are you sure we should print this?"
It's Monday. I'm dealing with my regular progress reports.
Perhaps I should have seen this coming, but Hamada-san responded to the email containing my interview article with a very difficult expression.
"…I'll check with Touma Youko Office, of course. Though I don't think there will be any problems as far as I'm aware."
I did hesitate at least three times before sending the files containing the text, though…
Even so, this is my job as an employee.
"…We might be better off converting this to a book or a movie script. I'm sure we'd be able to produce the bestseller of the week with this."
Naturally, this is the inevitable result of going to the entertainment industry with material like this.
Right now, the name Touma Kazusa is many times more valuable than she herself thinks.
…Just like the name Touma Youko, she might still be the talk of the town for decades to come, though only time will tell.
"Hey, that girl and her mother are on good terms, right?"
"Appearances aside, they're connected by a deep, genuine bond deep down."
"…Normally it'd be the opposite."
But this is about Touma Youko and Touma Kazusa.
Two uncooperative people overflowing with talent. Two good people with questionable personalities.
Completely different from what us normal people would consider to be a parent-child relationship.
"But this article must be written with a lot of prudence. Otherwise, it'll look like nothing more than a sensational exposition article."
"…You're right."
"I do feel that this has strayed a bit from what we and Ensemble were aiming for…"
Putting Kazusa's words into writing without alteration results in an article oozing with an astonishing amount of degrading intent.
Without translating her expression, tone… and all her complicated and concealed feelings into writing, all the nuance disappears…
This is bound to cause anyone who doesn't know her to misunderstand her.
Particularly, the locals who will read the article expressing the particular Japanese she uses when she's in a bad mood.
"I don't intend on letting this article end up as nothing more than a gossip article either."
I'll have to translate it for them.
That's a job only I'm capable of.
Youko-san asked me to do this job because I'm the only one capable of it.
…For her daughter's sake, she sacrificed everyone but her daughter.
"I'll write not just about what she said on the surface, but what Touma Kazusa truly feels."
That's why I'll have to expose everything.
I'll have to expose that Touma Kazusa is, in fact, a pure girl who cries a lot and is easily hurt deep down despite her unwelcoming facade.
"I see… Well, if you're going that far, I'll watch over silently a bit longer. For the time being, I'll review this with the other party."
"Please do. Thank you."
If she says that there's only a week left, I'll dig everything up before then.
If she says it's goodbye when that time comes, then I'll expose everything.
I'll engrave everything about her into my heart.
So I'll never forget her again. So I can remember her even if she's not next to me.
Don't underestimate me, Kazusa…
"Here, take this."
"…!? T-This is…"
"I have two, so if you want to take Takeya-kun along… No, please do invite Takeya-kun."
"Touma-san's… concert."
"Our company is really accommodating with events like these. Though it looks like the ordinary tickets sold out immediately."
"But how could you get your hands on these? Setsuna, don't tell me these are your own…"
"Yes, I planned on going myself… along with Haruki-kun."
"…Did you invite Haruki?"
"No, something prevented me from going before I could invite him… I have a business trip in Kansai at the end of this week. This is my first job entrusted to me alone."
"I-I see! So that's how it is."
"It's not like I can just say no… but I always hoped for something like this. If I said no now, I might never get a chance for a job like this again."
"Yes, yes, you always wanted to go on one, Setsuna. You seemed really jealous of Haruki's overseas business trip."
"Though I can't be satisfied by just going on one. I have to achieve good results like Haruki-kun too."
"That's great, good luck. I'm jealous that you have the opportunity to work a job you like. As far as that is concerned, I…"
"A-Anyway, let's talk about work later. So, will you accept these?"
"…I don't mind going, but could you hand Takeya's yourself?"
"Why? What does it matter who I give them to if you're both going?"
"Of course it matters. Are you telling me to invite Takeya? …That's far too difficult for me, Setsuna."
"…Complicated as always, you two."
"Yes, yes… then I'll take that as an okay. Huh? Yes, I see… Hey, Io, he asked where the two of you should meet up."
"Let him decide by himself…"
"…He said that if he can decide by himself, then he'll pick you up at your apartment at 10 o'clock in the morning. You'll go shopping, dine and rest a bit before the concert…"
"Half past five in front of the concert hall! Don't add pointless options!"

"Ah, sorry to keep you waiting! Yes, yes, just as you thought, Takeya-kun, she wants to meet up 30 minutes before the performance at the concert hall. Amazing, it's like you can read each other's minds."
"Yes, I'll give the tickets to Io. I hope you'll enjoy the concert, then… Oh no, I'm sorry for all the trouble. See you."
"…With that settled, here are the tickets."
"…Alright, since I have no choice now."
"I'm happy for you. Takeya-kun said yes."
"The things that idiot told you… He hasn't changed a bit after all."
"The things…? What things?"
"You know, the umm… break and all."
"Aah, that? He was just talking about taking a break at a cafe, you know? I'm sure you're the one overthinking things, Io."
"This is Takeya we're talking about. There is no overthinking things when he is concerned!"
"But… isn't it okay for you two to start overthinking things by now?"
"…Did Haruki tell you to say that?"
"No, not really… I haven't seen him much lately."
"…What's the matter with you two? Whenever I ask Haruki about this, he only ever gives me vague answers."
"Like I said, it's no big deal…"
"Um… I might be overstepping, but could it have something to do with Touma-san…?"
"No, it doesn't."
"I sure hope so… but you were all over him recently."
"Sorry for lying…"
"Regardless, what's with you wanting to go to her concert after all this time? And with Haruki, no less."
"I couldn't go in the end, though."
"Had I known, I would have absolutely stopped you. Why would you reopen old wounds after all this time? There's nothing to be gained by doing that, you know?"
"…She's my friend."
"Setsuna…"
"That's why it's alright even if I could only see her from afar. I wanted to see Kazusa. I wanted to meet the real Kazusa one more time."
"She might not forgive me. She might still not have given up on him. We might not be friends anymore because of that, but…"
"But… I can't go anymore."
"Not going is the correct choice. Besides, you have work, so it's not like you have a choice."
"Is it really the correct choice?"
"Haruki would obviously refuse too. After all, there's just no way he would enjoy it."
"I might have been going around in circles. I might have been utterly incapable of reading the mood… I might have been overpresumptious."
"Forget about that girl already. All the happy memories, all the painful memories, all of it."
"In the end it doesn't matter if I go to the concert or not, our feelings will never change, will they…?"
"That's right. There's nothing that can get between you two anymore. You'll be able to find happiness with Haruki this time."
"When I said 'our'… I didn't mean the two of us."
"Setsuna…?"
"They will never change, will they…? Maybe they never did change all this time…"
"…What are you looking at?"
"Nothing…"
Her genuine sleeping face lasted for no more than two or three minutes.
"Peeking at people without restraint when they're sleeping… This is why I can't stand the mass media…"
"We're in the middle of an interview. I don't see any problems, though."
"And you have a way with words… You're really too much to handle."
Perhaps because she feels ashamed for having fallen asleep, or because she dislikes everything about this, she furrows her brows and throws words of indignation at me.
…She doesn't realize that the discrepancy between those two sides of her is what makes her attractive, and that unawareness is what makes Kazusa who she is.
"Huaaah… Where were we?"
"I can go home for today if you're sleepy."
"But then you'll come back tomorrow, won't you?"
"Well, until I'm done with my coverage."
"Then continue. Get it over with already and leave."
Her recent catchphrase of "it's for both our sakes" hasn't appeared tonight.
Maybe she's holding back because I always look uncomfortable when she says it, or perhaps those words make her uncomfortable too.
"Where were we…? Oh, right, we were talking about my five years in Vienna… About how many times men made advances on me."
I wouldn't have minded if she forgot about that topic.
"What, do you doubt me? Do you think there's no way that I'm popular with men?"
"That's not it, but…"
I found it hard to retort because I knew she wasn't lying, and that's probably the reason she felt sleepy in the first place…
"Compared to where I lived, lots of men approached me when I was on concert tours with my mom… Especially in France."
"I see…"
"Paris used to be mom's base of activity, so I get plenty of attention by being 'Touma Youko's daughter'… though not as much as in Japan."
"Yeah…"
"Anyway, there was this independent conductor. A Frenchman in his mid thirties… Apparently he was mom's lover when he was young."
Kazusa looks at me intently while speaking, then laughing as if she's drunk.
"I thought he already had both money and status thanks to mom, yet he had the nerve to flirt with me. Was he trying to get lucky with both mother and daughter?"
"When we were dancing at a party, he whispered dirty things in my ear. About wanting to be alone with me, or about how I looked exactly like Youko when she was young."
It's like she's enjoying seeing me avert my gaze further and further.
"He said something about wanting to return the favor he owed Youko to me. That he'd let me play the piano as part of his orchestra… in exchange for the key to my room."
She looks like she's having a blast seeing me grit my teeth.
"He was getting on my nerves, obviously, so I kicked him between his legs the moment the song ended."
"…! …Aaaah."
And when I breathe a sigh of relief in the end, she looks sorrowful as if hit with a painful realization.
"I couldn't cool my anger for a while, but mom kept laughing all night. She told me that these things are men's dreams, so I should let him off the hook."
"I… I see."
"He's still a standing member of the Paris orchestra. Should I tell you his name? He might even be my father."
"N-No… We won't be able to print this anyway."
"Hmm…"
"So, any impressions?"
"…Nothing in particular."
"…Why are you so blunt? I told my favorite story. Don't Japanese people like things like this?"
"…Perhaps."
Except me, that is.
"…Could it be that you're shocked?"
"Like I said, nothing in particular."
If you know already, then don't talk about things like this.
…Well, I bet she's bringing up this kind of topic precisely because she knows.
"Hmm～"
Kazusa leans forward on her knees and brings her face closer, as if to carefully inspect my averted gaze.
Even though she was really against the idea of me sitting next to her up until now.
"Well, you know, Haruki… You're not suited to be part of the mass media."
"I had that painful realization just now…"
"Haha, hahaha… You really haven't changed even after five years. You should've become a prosecutor or something instead."
The reason I feel hurt isn't because the topic is imprudent…
Kazusa didn't push the topic any further, satisfied with having outdone me.
"But in the end, no one managed to attract me…"
"After all, I was completely different from mom. I usually looked at men with hostility, so I couldn't really mingle with them."
Kazusa's eyes returned to a more frank tone.
"Men like that will give up right away when I hurt their pride by throwing a good insult at them."
But rather than having lightened up, it looks more like she's just sleepy again. So the light in her eyes is periodically covered by her eyelids.
"Men who were too rich to bother with me. Men who were so poor that they tried to make up for it with their pride, so they couldn't stand my attitude…"
So I'm not sure if she has noticed…
At some point, she started to gently speak of her past as if singing a calming lullaby to me.
"Ah, right… there were tons of men who had as little talent as they had money."
"You have all of those in plenty. Money, talent… and pride."
"That's right, I'm the same as them. I'm human garbage with overly high pride, and there is no value in being near me, nor in making advances on me."
"That's not…"
"I started thinking that… there's probably only one man in the world who keeps getting close to me no matter how many times I push him away."
"Eh…"
"Ah, s-sorry. Forget what I just said."
"No, it's nothing…"
"…Forget about that. I'm really sorry."
Why is she apologizing?
If she just let it pass, it wouldn't be so obvious who she was referring to.
"Haaah, mh, mh…"
"Come on, put your arms under the sheets too."
"Mh…"
"Haaah… mh… ah…"
After that, Kazusa rested her chin on her hands at some point.
After her head fell down on her arms twice, she completely lost consciousness.
That's why I have no choice. I really have no choice.
I hold Kazusa in my arms, carry her to the bed, put the sheet over her, and look at her as she sleeps.
Because I had no choice.
"Mh… nh…"
Just like when she was taking a nap earlier, her sleeping face is pure and genuine.

"I've always looked at you with envy as you fly around the country, doing your best, Haruki-kun. Perhaps with this, I can catch up to you a little bit?"
"I want to give you a souvenir when I'm back from my business trip. That's why I'm thinking of calling you on Monday."
"Let me talk about all kinds of things when that time comes. If possible, I want to reconcile too."
"Now then, I'll be doing my best on my business trip. I won't work any less hard than you, Haruki-kun."
"Since that's how it is, I won't be in Tokyo this Sunday, so I won't be able to attend Kazusa's concert."
"You said you weren't going, Haruki-kun, but I actually managed to get some tickets. I was planning on going to listen to Kazusa play."
"If possible, I wanted to go with you, Haruki-kun."
"You might be wondering why I'd decide something like that on my own. You might even be angry at me."
"I'm sorry. But if I was going, I absolutely needed you with me. Because…"
"I didn't want you… to go to Kazusa's concert alone, Haruki-kun."
"Because I know how you will feel if you go to listen to Kazusa's performance alone."
"Your heart will leave me and it'll be sucked in by her playing. I know that."
"This is no good…"
"If I send this, I'm sure Haruki-kun will be…"
"But…"
"I want to take a picture of you playing…"
"Didn't I tell you earlier? I'm savoring the experience until the concert."
"Like I said, you can just pretend to be playing."
"You're persistent, Haruki. Hold back for two more days."
"…Fine."
It's not like I want to hear her piano right now, I just want to take a picture of her in that pose…
Whether Kazusa knows that or not, she's trying to distance me from her piano.
"Then go toward the window this time. Look out through the window."
"There won't be an idiot dangling from the window sill, will there?"
"…Who knows."
Music Room 2.
The room that was occupied by a single student five years ago. One of the seven mysteries of the school, and the room that no one dared to enter.
The cold winter breeze blows in through the open window, swaying Kazusa's long hair.
I don't let that photo opportunity go past me, so I take a picture from the side right when Kazusa holds back her hair.
"It's cold…"
"It's going to be below freezing tonight too. Keep yourself warm when you go to sleep tonight."
In Music Room 2, where the heater has long since been turned off, the freezing air envelops the room in an instant.
Outside the window are the sports clubs about to wrap up their exercise, and the sky slowly changing from red to dark blue.
A spectacle is unfolding, one that's identical to what happened two years ago… One that hasn't changed at all since five years ago.
The only difference is the girl who wasn't here two years ago, but who was here five years agoーand how she looked different back then.
"…Okay, you can close it now."
"No, it's fine."
"Didn't you hate the cold?"
"It's fine…"
Kazusa shivers from the cold… but the cold most likely isn't the cause behind her crumbling expression.
"Hey, Haruki."
"Hm?"
"Today… is the last day of your coverage, right?"
"You'll be rehearsing all day tomorrow, and your concert is the day after that. I can't be dragging you out with me any more than this."
"You're right…"
Due to our time together ending at the end of this week like Kazusa decided, today must be the day everything ends.
"This'll be the last time."
"Yeah…"
"You really are vulgar. To think that even at the very end, you'd take me to the number one place I want to forget."
"See, you just admitted it. This place is 'number one' for you."
I always planned to bring Kazusa here no matter how she felt about it.

"This is the place you spent the most time in during your three years at this school… probably more than your time spent in the classroom."
"I was really irritated during my time here. I kept stamping my feet in frustration because nothing ever went well."
…Though perhaps my only mistake is that this place is too appropriate.
"You keep saying that, but the music you played in your irritation gave me the impression that you had a lot of fun."
"There was this crappy guitarist who could never match up to me no matter how much time passed… That only added to my irritation."
While saying that, Kazusa clicks her tongue with a hint of nostalgia.
"…I'm sorry."
…I do think her expression is a bit strange, but that's how she really is, so it can't be helped.
"Did you get a bit better? Did your skills improve enough that you can play along with others?"
"Even five years ago I could do that…"
"Oh, I know! How about you play for me? Look, there is a guitar there."
"I think I'll pass…"
"What's the problem? I'll only laugh, but I won't instruct you on every little thing."
"Usually it's the opposite."
"A single song is fine. You can even play Romance de Amor if you want."
"I said I can't. I haven't played once ever since I got a job."
"Why won't you play for me? Does Setsuna have exclusive rights to listen to you playing the guitar?"
"…I never said that."
Even if that is true.
I don't know what Kazusa just discerned, but this time she clicks her tongue with a hint of sadness.
…I wish she wouldn't make that expression.
Choosing this place was definitely not a mistake, yet I'm starting to regret it.
"Aa-ah… What an unaccommodating man."
With a sigh Kazusa puts her hands on the window frame, and then turns back to me.
"If you're going to be so stubborn, then I have an idea of my own."
"Don't get angry… about something like this."
Her hair that was blowing backwards earlier is now blowing in her direction, brushing gently against her cheeks.
Gently, just like Kazusa's current expression…
"This is… the last time. This will mark the end, so I can tell you everything now, right?"
But her voice is as cold as the wind blowing against her hair.
"This isn't really the end…"
"We won't ever meet again, so I can cross the line just a little bit, right?"
The words "of course not" refuse to leave my mouth.
This isn't the end. She has an additional concert to play… She might even return to Japan again sometime.
Am I just trying to contradict Kazusa's resigned feelings? Or am I perceiving a different meaning behind her enigmatic smile?
That uncertainty was cleared up the next time Kazusa opened her mouth.
"Hey, Haruki… You kissed Setsuna for the first time on that day we were on the stage, right?"
At that moment, all I could do was desperately grasp after the camera that fell from my hands.
"That night, right here… This is where Setsuna confessed to you, where you two kissed… and where you two became lovers, right?"
"H-H-H…Hey! What's this about all of a sudden?"
My voice ended up betraying me because of how sudden that statement was and just how unlike her it was to make it.
"I'm talking about five years ago… That day five years ago when everything ended."
Kazusa is smirking.
She's letting out a vague smile that can be seen as proof of either malice, a desire to tease, or countless other emotions.
"N-N-No… That's, um…"
"If I'm wrong, you can deny it. But if you're going to lie, then make sure it's not an obvious one."
"L-Like I told you, back then… I was the one who confessed…"
No matter how much anyone tries to press the matter, I just can't admit the fact that it was Setsuna who confessed to me, which would make nobody happy…
"Doubtful. As if you had the guts to do something like that back then… You were completely indecisive between Setsuna and me."
"T-That's not…!"
"That's not… true."
Look… Not even Kazusa is happy to hear about it.
That's why I just can't admit it.
"Since it's you we're talking about, that was probably your first kiss too, right? You could never initiate something like that yourself after all."
"Wha… What's wrong with that?"
I have no clue about the reason behind Kazusa bringing this up.
Why would she decide to talk about the day of our first separation… in the middle of what should be our final meeting?
Besides, that wasn't just my first time back then. Setsuna too had never…
"…Haha. Ahah, hahahahaha!"
"Well, what's so funny…?"
Even though she's not happy in the slightest, she lets out an empty laugh.
"It's as I thought… Setsuna must've been looking. She saw me."
"Setsuna saw… what?"
Just when I'm on the brink of losing all understanding, she throws an insinuating line at me like she's doing it on purpose.
"I always thought that might have been the case; that perhaps that was the reason Setsuna did as she did… I suppose you could call this the shock of realizing a five-year-old truth?"
"I don't understand it at all… What in the world are you…?"
I'm sure she's doing this to mess with me, but the atmosphere she has created is far too pitiful.
"There's no point in telling you now… but since this is the last time, it's fine, right?"
"Don't come to your own conclusions! What's so wrong about that? What's so funny? …Why are you talking about Setsuna that way?"
That's why I'm the one who's irritated right now.
"No, there's nothing wrong with it… Nor is it funny… Setsuna didn't do anything wrong either."
As she mutters those words, Kazusa takes a nearby chair and puts it in front of me. Then she sits down on the piano chair for some reason.
Unable to understand anything, I nervously sit down on the chair Kazusa prepared for me…
"I just think that it's a shame. Not for me, nor for Setsuna… but for you, Haruki."
"For me…? Why…?"
"All your first experiences were with me. That really must be the worst… Serves you right."
"…What…?"
I am left completely bewildered by Kazusa's nonsensical confession.
"It means that your past is defiled by me near every corner. Just like that night during the graduation ceremony, or that time at the airport the next day…"
The path I chose.
And the path I turned away from, despite knowing that doing so is a mistake…
"I'm sorry for toying with you all this time… despite being a woman with no ties to your future."
Kazusa denies my sin as if my divergence from the correct path was a trap laid by her.
"…I have no idea what you've been talking about up until now."
"Then can I tell you from here on out? You won't regret hearing it?"
If you're going to ask in that way, then don't look so insinuating…
"Tell me…"
With Kazusa's insinuation firmly on my mind and expressed on my turned face, I urge Kazusa forward.
Though with my face turned, my intention can never be conveyed to Kazusa.
"Back then… I was playing the piano here like always."
"No… it wasn't quite like always. I was more irritated than usual because I had been forced to wear a thin and skimpy outfit."
"Ah…"
When Kazusa said "from here on out," she wasn't talking about the future, but the past.
About that day we were on the stage.
"As I was doing that, the usual nuisance came into the room. No matter how many times I chased him out, he never learned his lesson and came back. What a stubborn person he was."
A short while after our song was met with roaring applause…
The exhilaration from my time on the stage wouldn't go away, so as I was walking around the school hallways immersed in the aftertaste of our concert, I heard a melody from the usual music room.
"I was feeling more irritated than usual, yet he didn't know about my feelings, so he started talking to me, getting all excited by himself."
When I opened the door, the person I wanted to see the most was inside.
"He was more annoying than usual, so I answered him half-heartedly. But despite that, he wouldn't stop talking."
That's because I was happier than usual. It didn't matter if her answers were half-hearted; I just kept talking to her.
About how I wanted to stay like that forever. With the three of us.
She rejected that idea from a rational standpoint, but I kept on telling her about my egotistical dream.
"At some point I stopped hearing his voice. When I turned around, I saw that he had dozed off while still sitting."
Because I had gone through countless all-nighters…
"Yes, he was sleeping. Around the same time as right now."
Because of that, our memories after this point diverge.
The next time I reopened my eyes, Setsuna was suddenly right in front of me, and…
"I only got more annoyed… I thought about giving him a piece of my mind, so I went to him."
But it's not Setsuna who's here right now.
It's not Setsuna, but Kazusa who's standing up from her chair, and slowly walking toward me.
"I went closer to him, then leaned forward to take a closer look at his face. He was facing down, so I had to do it like this, from below…"
She comes closer to me, then she leans forward to take a closer look at my face. With undiluted eyes, she looks at me from below…
"And then right before my eyes, I saw his incredibly defenseless and half-witted face… Yes, just like right now."
"…What are you…"
"Don't move!"
"Don't move… Otherwise, this won't be a repeat of back then."
Right now, Kazusa is in the exact same posture Setsuna was in back then.
It's as if she knows what happened here five years ago. No, it's as if she saw what happened here five years ago.
"Otherwise, I won't be able to show you what I did after this."
No, no, that's wrong, that's wrong too. There's no way Kazusa could've seen what happened back then.
Then who did…?
Who saw Kazusa when she was here back then?
The moment that thought enters my head… I can see the awaiting future… as well as the past.
The scene that I didn't see… and the scene that Kazusa and Setsuna did see.
"I was the one who did it first… I was the first one."
"Kazu…sa…!"
Kazusa's palms touch my cheeks.
This, too, might be a reenactment of what happened five years ago… of those few minutes before I woke up.
"Kissing him, making love to him… and falling in love with him."
"I knew that it was cowardly… and unforgivable."
Kazusa's breath touches me every time she speaks.
"But there was no way I could confess to him. I hated myself so much, so I thought that there was no way he'd fall in love with me."
Kazusa's lips come close enough to nearly touch mine.
"That's why I did something so awful and so fitting of me. That's how much I was at my wits' end. It hurt so much."
Kazusa's expression is now all that is visible within my field of vision.
"…I didn't want anyone else to steal him away."
I sense a sweet scent coming from Kazusa's body.
It's a scent that shakes me to my core, to the point that I'm unable to explain it away by saying that it's just because she likes sweet food.
"But Setsuna stole him that very day. Setsuna took everything."
Kazusa's voice resounds in my chest.
Along with her pitiful words that in utter contrast to her sweet scent make me grimace.
"After all, I didn't think it was possible… That there'd be another weird woman like me…"
It hurts so much.
The way she makes me falsely believe through her words and movements that nothing has changed these past five years hurts so much.
"That such a good person, such a good woman… would have such terrible taste in men. Who could have possibly known that…?"
The way she cried as she lamented to me five years ago hurts too…
As well as the way she's making me falsely believe that her warmth, coldness, sadness, and pitifulness haven't deteriorated one bit since that night we parted.
"Haruki, Haruki…"
"Stop… it."
When I see Kazusa's eyes slowly water right in front of me, I let out a voice that proves that my own eyes are doing the same thing.
"You're messing with me, right? You're trying to get even for what I've done, right? That's what this is… tell me that it is."
It's because I'm sad.
I'm sad because, while my time has moved forward, Kazusa's time has remained stagnant. A divergence between our paths that's so decisive.
At least… that divergence was supposed to have taken place.
"Do you think… this is a joke? Are you going to laugh this off as a joke, even when I'm telling you all this, Haruki?"
"Of course I can't laugh it off… So I'm begging you, laugh at it for me."
At that moment…
I can feel a single drop fall upon me from Kazusa's wet eyes.
"If you don't laugh it off, I won't know what to do…!"
"You can't do anything anyway. Don't talk so thoughtlessly about not knowing what to do when it's already too late…!"
"Then don't thoughtlessly talk about this either if it's too late! If today is our last day, then you should have carried that knowledge with you to the grave!"
"…Haruki… Haruki, Haruki… you're cruel."
"You're… you're the one… who's cruel… Kazusa… You're the one…"
Her forehead bumps against mine.
The tip of her nose lightly hits mine.
Her tears go down even my cheeks.
"This is the last time, so…"
"I'll never acknowledge that."
"All that is left is the concert. Everything'll be fine. We'll never be alone together after this."
"I just said I'll never acknowledge that!"
"If I just hold your hand… If I just tell you my feelings… If I just kiss you once more and for the last time…"
"Setsuna would forgive that much, right?"
My vision turns to darkness. My eyes are shut.
Because… Kazusa closed her eyes.
"Haruki… Haah, aah…"
"Kazusa…!"
And then I feel a warm and soft sensation on my lips…
But I only felt it for a single moment.
It was my cell phone that was flashing the moment I opened my eyes.
Even if it's only spam mail, the timing of which it was sent was far too miraculous and precise, and it was both great and awful at the same time.
"It's Setsuna."
"Why…"
"Why now, Setsuna…?"
The name of the sender far transcends any mere coincidence…
"Why didn't you stop me earlier…?"
1. I avert my gaze.
2. I look her in the eyes.
"Look at me."
"Do you hate me that much?"
"Don't ask… such an unfair question."
I feel Kazusa's breath on my right cheek.
"…But if you say anything more, I might actually try hating you."
But I desperately eject those lips and eyes from my field of vision.
"I might do my best to hate you."
Physically, I know that I'm only giving a fleeting resistance, but I imagine as far as my attitude goes, it's at least stronger than that…
"…I'm sorry."
Kazusa was the one to finally submit.
"I really am… hopeless, aren't I? I'm completely hopeless."
"That's not…"
With her hands still on my shoulders, she distances herself from me.
"You're right, it was a joke. I'm just messing with you. I tried to get back at you, Haruki."
Along with excuses that come far too late… which no one would ever believe.
"Although, it failed completely until the very end… You really don't know how to spot a joke."
…Her eyes redden, yet she still shows me an indecipherable smile.
"So, you know, this marks the end of our last interview… Good work."
She's trying to act strong in front of me, and she's being considerate of Setsuna.
And she's harboring a strange feeling that's neither quite resigned nor sad.
"Mn…"
And then I feel a warm and soft sensation on my lips…
"…I'm sorry, Haruki."
But I only felt it for a single moment.
"I really am… hopeless, aren't I? I'm completely hopeless."
"Kazusa…?"
With her hands still on my shoulders, she distances herself from me.
"You're right, it was a joke. I'm just messing with you. I was getting back at you, Haruki."
Along with excuses that come far too late… which no one would ever believe.
"As proof of that… Haha, hahaha. Look, I'm laughing, am I not?"
…Her eyes redden, but her smile is probably from the heart.
"So, you know, this marks the end of our last interview… Good work."
She's trying to act strong in front of me, and she's being considerate of Setsuna.
Along with a happiness within Kazusa from having a miniscule wish granted.
"Come to the concert… okay?"
We were both completely silent on the way home… until Kazusa finally opened her mouth during our parting.
"It's enough that you come. All you have to do is listen to me play the piano."
"Kazusa, I…"
"…Since it's you we're talking about, you'll probably fall asleep halfway through out of boredom though."
Kazusa continues speaking as if to prevent me from letting out my words of indecisiveness.
"I'll stay in a hotel close to the concert hall from tonight on. I'll only be thinking about the concert these last two days."
"I see."
"Once the concert is over, I'll have an associate come to fetch my luggage… I won't be returning to that apartment anymore."
Kazusa shows me a light smile.
It's as if the feelings inside her heart have no bearing on her smile.
"That's why, this time… is our final farewell."
And then, once again… she persistently makes the same declaration that she has undone countless times herself, and which also has been undone by me.
"Goodbye then."
And perhaps because we've already shared countless final farewells already, Kazusa's last parting words come off as thoughtlessly cold.
"I was the one who did it first… I was the first one."
What are you saying after all this time?
"Kissing him, making love to him… and falling in love with him."
It's too late now.
"…I didn't want anyone else to steal him away."
Had she… told me that five years ago, I would have…
I would have…
No, nothing would have changed. Nothing can be allowed to have changed.
"Haruki, Haruki…"
Stop it…
"This is the last time, so…"
To cross an even farther line than what I initially desired under the pretense that it would be the last time…
To engrave a feeling within the both of us that we can never forget…
"If I just hold your hand… If I just tell you my feelings… If I just kiss you once more and for the last time…"
Why does today have to be the last…?
This shouldn't be the end. We should go more slowly…
Does there not exist a choice within you to sublimate our relationship as friends…?
Are 1 and 0 the only choices when it comes to me…?
"Setsuna would forgive that much, right?"
"Aaaaah!"
"Haah, haah, aaah…!"

…But not even 30 minutes have passed since I last checked the time.
And here I was thinking that I finally managed to fall asleep.
"…! Haah, haah, haah…"
Ever since Kazusa's farewell, that same scene has repeated itself in my mind.
That unbearable, pitiful and beautiful scene.
"Glug, mng… aah!"
In order to chase that thought from my mind, I exhausted every alcoholic drink in the room, which only served to make the image more vivid.
Her voice, her breath, her expression, and even her thoughts that should be unknown to me. I added those details in a way that was convenient to me.
…No, in a way that was very inconvenient for me.
I gulp some cold tea down my sore throat to desperately cool my head.
One moment I prepare the tea cold, and then I prepare it hot the other. Even I think my actions are not making sense.
For a while now, I've been trying to find the best way to stop myself from thinking through trial and error.
Yet despite that…
The response from my mind and body is terrifying. My wavering heart despises the actions I take against my instincts.
A feeling of exhaustion is overwhelming my body. A result of my extreme emotions and feelings of pleasure that stem from my mistakes.
The proof of my violently shifting emotions is inside my underwear.
I thought about Kazusa… I thought of someone other than Setsuna.
All because I closed my eyes for a few minutes.
